explainBack.question: Why would drawing a rough sketch and placing a comment on one area produce a better result than writing a single longer, more detailed prompt?
explainBack.answer: Because words describe spatial layout ambiguously while a sketch supplies the arrangement directly—the system receives a rough map of where the sofa, headline space or product should sit. A comment then bounds the edit to a small target (this sleeve, that lamp), so the regeneration is constrained to the intended region instead of the model reinterpreting the whole scene from a long verbal description. The limit still holds: the output is a newly generated image, not an editable file, so exact text and measurements need checking outside the picture.

explainBack.assessment: The article's mechanism fully supports this causal answer in ordinary language, including the crucial limit; explain-back passes.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A charity volunteer must revise last year's fundraiser poster: move the date banner to the top, replace the photo of the retiring organiser with the new one, and keep the logo and ticket price untouched—using ChatGPT Images 2.5 if it has appeared in her account.
unseenTransfer.question: Using the article's mechanism, how should she guide the tool, and what must she verify before printing?
unseenTransfer.answer: She should sketch the new layout first (banner top, photo position, logo corner) to give the system the spatial map, then make one targeted comment edit at a time—swap the photo, then move the banner—rather than one long prompt describing everything. Because the tool regenerates the image rather than editing layers, she must verify the date, ticket price and logo fidelity outside the finished picture before printing, and she should not assume the feature has reached her account or that her plan's generation limits allow unlimited attempts.
